clips.body: I went to therapy for years before I ever became a therapist. I know what it’s like to sit on the other side of the room and wonder if anyone really gets it. That’s why I work so hard to make sure every client here feels understood from the very first session.

Empathy is the core of my work, and here I get to bring my whole self into every session. Nobody asks me to rush or to treat people like numbers. That freedom makes me a better therapist, and my clients can feel the difference.

I spent nearly a decade in community mental health before I found a practice that protects its clinicians. My caseload here is balanced, I have time to prepare, and I actually leave work with energy left for my own family. That changes everything about the care I can give.

My reason for doing this began long before my career did: watching my dad struggle quietly for years. He never got the help he needed because it was too hard to find. Every time a new client tells me they almost didn’t call, I think about him.

What stands out here is how kind everyone is, to clients and to each other. We check in on one another after hard sessions, we celebrate wins together, and nobody is too busy to talk through a tricky case.
At Harbor Mind, we believe clients are never the problem. They just haven’t had the right support yet. Our job is to listen, find what fits, and keep adjusting until things start to feel lighter.
Doing it right here means doing it right every session, not just when someone is watching. It means being honest, being prepared, and always putting the client’s wellbeing ahead of convenience.

When I think about who this work is for, I picture the people I know who are quietly struggling. Friends, neighbors, people at church. If we can make it a little easier for even one of them to reach out, it’s worth it.
The work here feels purpose-driven, not paperwork-driven. We have support for the admin side, so I can spend my energy where it matters, with the person in front of me.
Watching a client graduate from therapy still stands out to me every single time. Seeing someone leave with tools they’ll use for the rest of their life is the best part of this job.
